title: HostedAPI ephemeral latency cliff runbook sketch
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working sketch of a condensed runbook and after-action notes for the class of incidents we internally call an "ephemeral latency cliff" on Hosted API streaming endpoints. These are short (1–10min) but very high-impact spikes in p50/p95/p99 for streaming connections where token emission stalls or batches suddenly balloon, leading to client reconnects and downstream 5xx cascades. Purpose: capture quick triage and mitigation guidance, short-term automations we can build, and follow-ups for SRE + Serving Runtime to instrument more reliably.

Context / why this doc:
- Several recent pages (April–May 2026) had fast, hard spikes that recovered before full postmortem writeups; we need a small operational playbook for oncall engineers to reduce blast radius and gather critical telemetry.
- Not a replacement for full postmortem; intended to sit in front of longer-root-cause analysis.

Observed pattern (summary):
- sudden jump in streaming-send latency; clients see long gaps between tokens or a long tail of last-token latency.
- no sustained CPU/GPU saturation signals on node metrics; network egress rates may be steady or slightly decreased.
- control-plane shows ephemeral increase in queueing/backpressure counters (Nats/queue depth) for specific tenant shards.
- downstream edge/multiplexers report connection stalls then reconnects -> transient 5xx burst.
- usually correlated with a prefix-hotspot or prefetch race (hypothesis).

High-level impact:
- duration: typically 30s–7m; severity: P0 if >5% customers affected or if key tenant SLAs violated.
- user-visible: streaming timeouts, truncated responses, higher client-side reconnects and perceived hallucinations (because context truncated).

Quick runbook (first 10 minutes):
1) Triage: confirm incident class
   - Check streaming p50/p95/p99 for the last 5m vs baseline (Grafana: hostedapi.streaming.latency.*). Is the spike sudden or ramping?
   - Look at active sessions by tenant: hostedapi.sessions.active_by_tenant and per-tenant error spikes.

2) Short-term mitigations (order matters):
   a) Route around: enable fallback to non-streaming (chunked) endpoint for the affected route/model if available. Command: "/ops/route-decider fallback enable --route <route> --reason "streaming-latency-cliff""
   b) Flow-control relief: temporarily lower max_concurrent_streams_per_host for the edge pool serving the shard. Change via Ops console or run: "curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/safe-config -d '{"edge_pool":"pool-1","max_concurrent_streams":8}'" (must coordinate with infra team).
   c) Disable prefetch (only when prefetch counters show heavy eviction): flip "prefetch.enabled" false for the shard via runtime toggle. Note: this increases per-request latency but reduces KV contention.

3) Evidence collection (parallel):
   - Capture a 5–10 min range from traces: hostedapi.stream.emit.latency, edge.conn.reconnects, kvcache.*. Export to S3 (ops-waveform namespace).
   - Save example wire logs for 3 affected sessions from the edge and runtime. Use correlation id from telemetry (X-Trace / request-id).
   - Snapshot node-level metrics (top 5 nodes by queue depth).

4) Communication:
   - Post initial incident summary to #sre-incident with impact estimates and mitigations applied. Use incident template.
   - If customer-facing SLA risk: alert CS / Solutions: ping @emily-cs and @sam-sales.

Root-cause hypotheses (to check):
- Hypothesis A: Prefetch / KV-cache prewarming race causes transient KV lease storms -> latency cliff. Evidence: spiky kvcache.acquire latencies and eviction rates.
- Hypothesis B: Scheduler coalescing breakdown at edge causing ephemeral head-of-line blocking for streams with long tail tokens (e.g., long-stop tokens). Evidence: sudden increase in coalescer.queue-length and per-acceptor backlog.
- Hypothesis C: Midchain backpressure amplification between edge and runtime due to inconsistent backpressure windows (recent change to RTT thresholds). Evidence: mismatched ack-window metrics between edge and runtime nodes.

Data we need to validate hypotheses (post-incident):
- per-tenant kv lease/acquire timeseries + correlated prefix distributions
- timeline of prefetch toggles / recent deployments (check GitHub PRs in last 24h)
- full traces for affected sessions showing span times through edge -> midchain -> runtime -> GPU

Temporary fixes we can script (mid-term, 1–2 weeks):
- Auto-disable prefetch on shard when kvcache.acquire p99 > X ms for Y seconds (operatorizable).
- Fast toggle in control-plane to force stream->non-stream fallback for routes by tag.
- Edge pool autoscale rule: if streaming token emission p95 > threshold for 30s, temporarily expand pool by one node and re-run runtime load-balancing.

Permanent engineering follow-ups (owner + ETA suggestions):
- Instrument: Add per-span token-emission timings in traces so we can pinpoint token-level stalls (ENG: serving-runtime; ETA: 2w). Owner: Omar Singh.
- Scheduler: harden coalescer safety checks to avoid queue reordering when a stream has large KV fetches (ENG: serving-runtime; ETA: 3w). Owner: Benji Morales.
- KV layer: implement lease backoff jitter and improved eviction telemetry (ENG: platform-engineering; ETA: 4w). Owner: Lena Park.
- Deploy canary for prefetch toggle to ensure we can roll it without harming throughput (ENG: release-engineering; ETA: 1w). Owner: Aisha Kapoor.

Playbook checklist (for oncall):
- [ ] Confirm streaming latency cliff (p95+p99) and affected tenants list
- [ ] Apply fallback route for affected route(s)
- [ ] If fallback unavailable, reduce edge concurrency for pool(s)
- [ ] Collect traces + wire logs and upload to incident S3 bucket
- [ ] Create JIRA SRE-4321 and attach evidence

Quick reference commands (ops safe-mode):
- Snapshot traces: "./ops-scripts/snapshot-traces --range=5m --service=hostedapi --tag=streaming_cliff --out=s3://ops-incident/4321/trace.json"
- Toggle prefetch: "curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/runtime-toggle -d '{"shard":"shard-23","prefetch.enabled":false}'"
- Route fallback: "/ops/route-decider fallback enable --route /v1/generate --model redwood-mini --reason streaming_cliff"

Open questions / risk notes:
- Will disabling prefetch cause a different class of latency problems for prefix-heavy workloads? (depends on prefix distribution; need perf test).
- Does fallback to non-streaming penalize customers with long outputs (we need to estimate token cost and user-impact)?
- Is there any interaction between our recent window-sizing change and specific edge NIC firmware versions? (Ops to correlate host images)

Post-incident reporting items (owner / ETA):
- SRE to write full postmortem tying traces to hypothesis (owner: Aisha, ETA: 1w).
- Serving Runtime to instrument token-level spans (owner: Omar, ETA: 2w).
- Release to schedule a canary for prefetch toggle (owner: release-eng, ETA: 1w).

Notes to self / fragments:
- Saw a case where a single tenant's prefix caused kv lease churn; tenant had huge fanout due to a chat-bot fanout pattern. Maybe we should add per-tenant fanout limits to prefetch.
- Consider an emergency "stream-ttl" fallback: if token emission stalls > X sec, close stream server-side with structured partial-continue error so clients can rehydrate.

Appendix: example timeline (from raw incident)
- 15:02:14 — small increase in coalescer.queue-length at edge-12, starts rising for 30s
- 15:02:46 — first client reconnects (trace id x-abc-001), streaming p95 jumps from 120ms -> 1.4s
- 15:03:05 — kvcache.acquire p99 spikes to 220ms for leader nodes in shard-23
- 15:03:20 — ops toggled prefetch=false for shard-23 (manual). Queues drained after ~90s.
- 15:04:50 — streaming p95 back near baseline, reconnect rate normalized by 15:05:10

End of draft.

Please comment inline with what we should make automated vs manual, and any missing telemetry you're relying on when you triage.
